title: TC-SAW (Temperature Compensated SAW) - Band 7 (2600 MHz) for Automotive V2X Communication
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Anya Krishnamurthy

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a TC-SAW (Temperature Compensated SAW) filter targeting Band 7 (2600 MHz) for Automotive V2X Communication. The filter is designed on AlN on Si substrate with a target center frequency of 1295.6 MHz and bandwidth of 336.6 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the Automotive V2X Communication module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: TC-SAW (Temperature Compensated SAW)
- Frequency Band: Band 7 (2600 MHz)
- Application: Automotive V2X Communication
- Substrate: AlN on Si
- Package: Fan-Out WLP
- Design Tool: COMSOL Multiphysics 6.2
- Design Center: Helsinki 5G Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the TC-SAW (Temperature Compensated SAW) design targeting Band 7 (2600 MHz). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       1295.6 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       336.6 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 2.9 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 19.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 38.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 38.0 dB
Q Factor:               13584
Temperature Coefficient:-8.3 ppm/°C
Die Size:               2.5 x 2.0 mm
Wafer Size:             8-inch
Number of Resonators:   6
Electrode Material:     Al
Passivation:            Si3N4
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open COMSOL Multiphysics 6.2 and load the TC-SAW (Temperature Compensated SAW) template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: AlN on Si with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 1295.6 MHz, BW 336.6 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 2.9 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (Fan-Out WLP).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (8-inch, AlN on Si).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Rohde & Schwarz ZNA67.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 3887 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 2.9 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 19.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 505 MHz offset >= 38.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 10 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 1.3 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +32 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 1000 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 93%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2025-05-09
Devices Tested:         23
Insertion Loss (meas):  2.64 dB
Return Loss (meas):     21.2 dB
Rejection (meas):       40.7 dB
Isolation (meas):       43.2 dB
Q Factor (meas):        13584
Group Delay Variation:  2.2 ns
Power Handling:         +34 dBm
Die Yield:              87.4%

Result Classification:  CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The TC-SAW (Temperature Compensated SAW) design demonstrated acceptable performance for Band 7 (2600 MHz).
b) Insertion loss is marginally above target; electrode thickness optimization recommended.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Slight frequency drift observed at +85°C; TC layer thickness may need adjustment.
e) No delamination observed after 1000-cycle thermal shock test.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
